title: S2f1 worker_control.steer: recorded steering messages delivered as interrupt plus resume for Codex threads and Claude sessions, original spec immutable (P13)
spec:
Extend orchestrator/worker_control.py with steer(task_id, message, *, reason, source="planner") -> dict. Record first: append {ts, task, reason, message, source} to .orchestrator/workers/<task>.steering.jsonl and a registry event steer (message length only in the event, the text lives in the steering file); bus event on the task (bus.update with an events entry if the bus supports it, else reason field untouched) and packet_meta.steering_count incremented; the task's spec, acceptance and scope are never modified. Delivery: registry status steering; interrupt the running process as cancel does but with hold skipped (SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL), then resume with the steering text prepended by 'Steering from <source> (<reason>):' and followed by 'The original task contract is unchanged.': Codex workers via executor.resume-style call on the recorded thread (see codex_reply and executor.argv_for kind resume; the worktree cwd selects the thread's worktree); Claude workers via spawn with the recorded packet_meta.session_id using claude -p --resume <session_id> (add a resume path to spawn.run_worker or a small spawn.resume_worker(task, prompt, session_id) that reuses the launch code, tools and env of the original role). When no session or thread is recorded, steer refuses with a clear error and leaves the worker running. Registry status back to running after resume with event steered. CLI: `orchestrator workers steer <task> --reason <text> --message <text>`. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md gains the steering section including the immutability rule.
Spec review T-1197 folded in: (1) Coordination with the interrupted worker's thread: the registry entry carries an integer epoch (starts at 1 on spawn); steer() increments it when it interrupts and records it on the entry; spawn and executor capture the epoch at launch and pass it to worker_registry.finish(task_id, ..., epoch=) and to their bus.post_result path, and finish() (scope adds orchestrator/worker_registry.py and tests/test_worker_registry.py) ignores a call whose epoch is older than the entry's, so the killed worker's late cleanup can never clobber the resumed run; the resumed run uses the new epoch. (2) worker_registry.FIELDS gains message_chars (int) for the steer event. (3) Codex delivery uses a dedicated executor.steer_resume(task, thread, message) that runs codex exec resume <thread> with the framed message directly (same access flags as argv_for kind resume), never executor.reply() and never resume_plan(), and does not touch the fix-loop rounds counter; a test asserts reply() is not called.
Spec review T-1210 folded in: (1) worker_registry.upsert(status='starting') carries the existing entry's epoch forward (and any explicit epoch kwarg wins), so a resumed launch that passes through the normal launch bookkeeping never resets it. (2) The epoch guard also covers capacity: executor.start's finally and spawn.run_worker release the pool reservation through worker_control.release_if_current(task_id, epoch, pool) which releases only when the epoch is still the entry's; the resumed run owns the reservation. (3) The interrupted thread's late bus writes are guarded without touching bus.py: steer() stamps pipeline.steer_epoch on the task; daemon._dispatch_worker (daemon.py joins the scope) and spawn.run_worker compare their launch epoch with pipeline.steer_epoch before bus.post_result/bus.update and skip when older. (4) Extract the SIGTERM/grace/SIGKILL loop from cancel() into worker_control._terminate(pid, *, grace_s, sleep, alive, signal_fn) used by both cancel() and steer(). (5) spawn records the effective tool allowlist of each launch (after any disclosure escalation) on the registry entry (field tools, list of names); resume_worker reuses that recorded list, not TOOLS[role].
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_worker_control.py::test_steer_records_before_delivery_and_never_edits_spec (steering file row, registry event, spec/acceptance/scope byte-identical)
tests/test_worker_control.py::test_steer_codex_resumes_thread_with_message (patched executor resume receives the thread id and the framed message)
tests/test_worker_control.py::test_steer_claude_resumes_session (patched Popen argv contains --resume and the session id)
